challenge_facts_addressed.effect_on_judgment: Two Alex-initiated one-on-one plans provide meaningful support for special interest, particularly the Saturday museum visit, but C1-F4 shows that Alex also makes one-on-one plans with other friends.

Remembering the presentation, sending encouragement, and bringing Jordan's preferred tea demonstrate personalized attention, though C1-F4 establishes that checking in and bringing treats are also part of Alex's broader friendly behavior.

Four extended private text conversations show sustained individual engagement and are the strongest evidence that Alex may have special interest, but they do not by themselves establish romantic intent.

reason_for_retaining_or_changing: B remains the primary conclusion, but with slightly reduced confidence after giving full weight to the repeated one-on-one initiation, personalized attention, and extended texting. Those facts support A, yet Alex's similar warmth and one-on-one engagement with others in C1-F4, the absence of explicit romantic signals in C1-F5, and the lack of follow-through after postponing dinner in C1-F6 still make general friendliness the better-supported interpretation.

revised_recommended_action.explanation: The evidence of individualized attention warrants remaining open to A, but the overall record does not yet clearly distinguish special or romantic interest from Alex's general friendliness.
